enhertu: EU approval came 395 days after the FDA's, and Italian reimbursement took another 896 days: 377 days longer than the median in this set and the 4th-longest wait of 27.
Germany rated its added benefit as considerable, one of the stronger results in the atlas, yet that did not secure fast access in Italy.
The EU approval was conditional. Conditionally approved drugs waited longest for Italian reimbursement in this set, so even strong German evidence did not shorten the wait.
lumakras: EU conditional approval came 223 days after the FDA. Italian reimbursement then took 870 days, the 6th-longest wait of 27.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group in its first decision, the same result as 13 of 29 drugs in the atlas.
Despite a US orphan designation, the drug had no orphan protection in Germany and was judged against existing therapy, where the evidence fell short.
trodelvy: The EU approved it 579 days after the FDA, the 4th-longest gap of 30.
Once approved in Europe, it was the fastest of all 27 reimbursed drugs in Italy: 260 days, 259 days under the median.
Germany rated its added benefit as major, one of only 2 drugs with the top rating. That fits the wider pattern: drugs Germany valued most also reached Italian patients faster.
pluvicto: EU approval followed the FDA's by 261 days. Italian reimbursement took 815 days, 296 days longer than the median.
Germany's verdict was split: considerable added benefit for one patient group, none proven for another.
A strong rating for part of the label did not prevent a long Italian process, the 9th-longest of 27.
retevmo: EU approval came 279 days after the FDA.
Italian reimbursement took 544 days, close to the median of 519.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group, despite the drug's US orphan designation: without orphan protection in Germany, it had to beat existing therapy.
carvykti: The EU approved this cell therapy 86 days after the FDA, one of the shorter gaps in the atlas.
Italy first classed it as not reimbursed. Reimbursement (class H) came 1,409 days after EU approval, the longest wait of the 27 reimbursed drugs.
Germany assessed it under orphan rules, where added benefit is deemed proven by law, and rated it non-quantifiable: benefit recognised, but not measured.
trikafta: Kaftrio reached EU approval 305 days after the FDA approved Trikafta.
Germany rated its added benefit as major, the top rating, given to only 2 of 29 drugs.
Italy reimbursed it in 318 days, 201 days faster than the median, and placed it in class A, one of 7 drugs in that class.
evrysdi: EU approval came 231 days after the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in 318 days, 201 days faster than the median.
Germany assessed it against existing therapy rather than under orphan rules: benefit was non-quantifiable for some patients and not proven for others.
zolgensma: This gene therapy was approved in the EU 360 days after the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in 299 days, the 2nd-fastest of 27 drugs.
Germany's first concluded decision, a full comparison triggered once sales passed the orphan threshold, found no added benefit. The same product got a fast Italian deal and a negative German verdict.
hemgenix: EU approval followed the FDA's by 90 days.
Italian reimbursement took 926 days, 407 days longer than the median and the 3rd-longest wait of 27.
Germany rated it non-quantifiable under orphan rules. Together with Carvykti, it shows that gene and cell therapies can face some of the longest Italian negotiations.
oxlumo: Approved in the EU 4 days before the FDA: effectively simultaneous.
Italian reimbursement took 501 days, close to the median of 519.
Germany assessed it under orphan rules, where benefit is deemed proven, and rated it non-quantifiable.
skyclarys: EU approval came 346 days after the FDA.
Italian reimbursement took 721 days, 202 days longer than the median. Earlier payment through Italy's Law 648/96 early-access list is not counted here.
Germany rated it non-quantifiable under orphan rules in its first decision.
voxzogo: The EU approved it 85 days before the FDA, one of 5 drugs approved in Europe first.
Italy reimbursed it in 382 days, 137 days faster than the median.
Germany rated it non-quantifiable under orphan rules. A re-assessment followed once sales passed the orphan threshold.
rinvoq: EU approval came 122 days after the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in 360 days, 159 days faster than the median.
Germany found considerable added benefit for at least one patient group, but no added benefit for others.
skyrizi: The US and EU approvals came 3 days apart.
Italy reimbursed it in 312 days, the 3rd-fastest of 27.
Germany found considerable added benefit, at its highest certainty level, for at least one patient group, though not for all.
tezspire: EU approval came 276 days after the FDA.
Italian reimbursement took 519 days, exactly the median of the set.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group, yet Italy reimbursed it in class A.
adbry: Approved in the EU, as Adtralza, 193 days before the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in 413 days, 106 days faster than the median.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group: reaching Europe first did not earn a better German verdict.
sotyktu: EU approval came 196 days after the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in 495 days, close to the median of 519.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group, the most common result in the atlas.
bimzelx: Approved in the EU 788 days before the FDA, the largest European lead in the atlas.
Italy reimbursed it in 453 days, 66 days faster than the median.
Germany found minor added benefit in both patient groups, one of 2 drugs with that rating.
rybelsus: EU approval came 196 days after the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in class A after 481 days, even though Germany found no added benefit.
It falls under Medicare's semaglutide negotiation: a Maximum Fair Price of $274 per 30-day supply from 2027, 71% below the $959 list price CMS reports.
wegovy: EU approval came 216 days after the FDA.
Italy has not reimbursed it: it remains in class C, 1,762 days after EU approval (as of 3 Nov 2026).
Germany has no benefit assessment, because statutory insurance excludes it as a lifestyle medicine, while in the US it shares the negotiated semaglutide Medicare price of $274.
mounjaro: EU approval came 125 days after the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in class A after 891 days, 372 days longer than the median.
Germany found minor added benefit for only one patient group and none for the rest. The German decision came 595 days after EU approval.
leqvio: Approved in the EU 378 days before the FDA.
Italian reimbursement (class A) took 663 days, 144 days longer than the median.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group: the European head start did not translate into fast Italian access.
camzyos: EU approval came 424 days after the FDA, the 6th-longest gap of 30.
Italian reimbursement took 854 days, 335 days longer than the median.
Germany found considerable added benefit, yet the Italian wait was still the 7th-longest of 27.
kerendia: EU approval came 222 days after the FDA.
Italy first classed it as not reimbursed, then reimbursed it in class A 842 days after EU approval.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group. Its decision came 547 days after EU approval.
leqembi: EU approval came 830 days after the FDA, the longest gap of all 30 drugs.
Italy had not reimbursed it 567 days after EU approval (class Cnn, as of 3 Nov 2026).
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group.
kisunla: EU approval came 449 days after the FDA, the 5th-longest gap of 30.
Italy had not reimbursed it 405 days after EU approval (class Cnn, as of 3 Nov 2026).
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group. Like Leqembi, it has had a slow European path for an Alzheimer's antibody.
vyepti: EU approval came 703 days after the FDA, the 3rd-longest gap of 30.
Italy reimbursed it in 522 days, close to the median of 519.
Germany found no added benefit for any patient group.
nurtec: Vydura reached EU approval 788 days after the FDA approved Nurtec ODT, the 2nd-longest gap of 30.
Italian reimbursement (class A) took 1,149 days, the 2nd-longest wait of 27.
Germany's first decision came 1,305 days after EU approval, the latest in the atlas, and found no added benefit.
vyvgart: EU approval came 236 days after the FDA.
Italy reimbursed it in 335 days, 184 days faster than the median.
Germany rated it considerable under orphan rules, the only orphan-route drug rated above non-quantifiable.
